subtitle: Mistral
rules_primary: If Mistral has the top-ranked LLM on Dec 31, 2024, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_secondary:
A tie would resolve to No. 

Clarification 3/14/24 6:03 PM ET: The Contract's Underlying states that, "The Underlying for this Contract is the Arena Elo rankings of large language models on the LMSYS Chatbot Arena Leaderboard as checked at 10:00 AM ET daily after Issuance and before <date>." To be clear, this refers to the "rank" column of the leaderboard, not the Arena Elo Score proper. As of this update, the #1 spot is tied between two variations of GPT-4 and Claude 3 Opus. Moreover, the Payout Criterion states that, "If they [the target organization] have an LLM that is tied with another LLM, then the Payout Criterion is not fulfilled." To be clear, if the only tie is with the same organization, that organization's strike would resolve to Yes. So if on the target date the tie is between two variations of GPT-4, then the market would resolve Yes in favor of OpenAI. However, if it is tied between GPT-4 and Claude 3, then both OpenAI and Anthropic's strikes would resolve to No.

subtitle: AI tool / AI
rules_primary: If A Company owned by Meek Mill releases an AI tool / AI to the public before Jan 1, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_secondary: For the purposes of this market, “Meek Mill” refers to the recording artist Robert Rihmeek Williams. The market will resolve Yes if any company that Meek Mill owns (whether a majority or minority equity stake in a private or directly-controlled company) commercially releases to the public an artificial intelligence tool or AI-powered feature before January 1, 2026. Passive investments such as holding stock in public companies (e.g., owning shares of Nvidia) do not qualify as ownership. A qualifying release must meet the Exchange’s definition of “commercial release”: the product is available for purchase, subscription, or download by the general public through official company channels, authorized retailers, or platform stores, and is not explicitly labeled as beta, early access, preview, prototype, or test. Ownership is established if Meek Mill has a direct equity stake in the company itself, verified through official company statements, corporate filings, or credible press reports from listed Source Agencies; endorsements, partnerships, or sponsorships without equity ownership do not qualify. Internal-only tools, announcements without public access, or purely promotional campaigns do not count. If at least one such company verifiably releases an AI product meeting these conditions before the deadline, the market resolves Yes; otherwise, it resolves No.

title: AI regulation by 2027?
subtitle: By Jan 1, 2027
rules_primary: If a bill becomes law regulating AI by Jan 1, 2027, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_secondary:
The bill must impose one of the following restrictions on products using large language models: forbid their creation; set limits on how they're trained, for example by limiting access to previously usable training data or by setting limits on the number of parameters they may be trained with; prevent their use for certain applications or uses, such as interacting with customers, interfacing with other applications, or performing actions on the web; or restrict the ability of US citizens to use foreign LLM-based products or restrict US operated LLM products or businesses from being sold to foreign customers or entities.

The export restriction must be specific, and not universally applied to all exports or exports of a broad industry. For example, a blanket ban on exports to a specific country would not qualify, and neither would a blanket ban on allowing the purchase of US businesses by investors in a specific country. Introducing a ban that specifically limits the export of artificial intelligence or machine learning software to a specific country or a broad number of countries would qualify if it was known to apply to LLM products. An introduced bill specifically classifying artificial intelligence software or machine learning models such that they would newly qualify for existing export bans would qualify.

title: Will Nvidia H200 chips being delivered to mainland China be confirmed?
subtitle: Before 2027
rules_primary: If Nvidia H200 chips being delivered to mainland China is confirmed by any of the Source Agencies after Issuance and before Jan 1, 2027, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_secondary:
This market resolves to Yes if any Source Agency confirms that one or more Nvidia H200 chips have been physically delivered to, received in, or imported into mainland China after Issuance and before Jan. 1, 2027.

For this market, “mainland China” means the People’s Republic of China excluding Hong Kong, Macau, and Taiwan. Delivery to Hong Kong, Macau, or Taiwan does not qualify unless a Source Agency confirms that the Nvidia H200 chips were subsequently delivered to, received in, or imported into mainland China.

Regulatory approval, export licenses, purchase orders, contracts, reservations, customer allocations, payment, revenue-recognition statements, manufacturing, packaging, shipment preparation, or statements of intent do not qualify unless a Source Agency confirms physical delivery, receipt, or import into mainland China.

References to Nvidia “H200,” “H200 AI chips,” “H200 GPUs,” “H200 processors,” “H200 accelerators,” or “H200 AI accelerators” qualify, provided the Source Agency is referring to Nvidia H200 chips. References only to other Nvidia chips, including H20, H100, B200, B300, Blackwell, or China-specific modified chips, do not qualify unless the Source Agency also confirms delivery of Nvidia H200 chips.

A report that Nvidia H200 chips were delivered to an approved Chinese customer outside mainland China will not qualify, unless a Source Agency confirms that those chips were delivered to, received in, or imported into mainland China before Jan. 1, 2027.

title: Will OpenAI release Astra before Aug 21, 2026?
subtitle: Before Aug 21, 2026
rules_primary: If OpenAI releases Astra before Aug 21, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_secondary:
Release must be to the public, outside of a closed beta, though limiting it to a high-cost subscription tier is acceptable.

On August 1, 2026, OpenAI publicly disclosed "Astra," an internal model described by OpenAI as its next major frontier system, citing results including the resolution of ten previously open mathematics problems - https://openai.com/index/ten-advances-in-mathematics/ 

Qualifying Release: The Payout Criterion is satisfied if OpenAI releases a model that either (a) is publicly named "Astra" (including numbered, lettered, or suffixed variants such as "Astra 1," "Astra 6," or "GPT-6 Astra"), or (b) is confirmed by OpenAI, or by a consensus of credible reporting, to share the same underlying model — including the same base architecture, weights, or training run — as the model referenced in OpenAI's August 1, 2026 disclosure, regardless of the commercial name, safety configuration, or access tier under which it is ultimately released. A separately-branded release that is derived from or built on the same underlying model as the disclosed Astra model satisfies this clause even if OpenAI markets it as a distinct product (e.g., a safety-restricted variant or a differently-priced tier), provided the shared underlying model is confirmed by OpenAI or by a consensus of credible reporting.

title: Will the US commit to a national AI regulator before Jan 1, 2028?
subtitle: Before Jan 1, 2028
rules_primary: If the United States agrees to or announces the establishment of a national AI regulator before Jan 1, 2028, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_secondary:
For this market, a qualifying establishment must be adopted through a law, executive order, regulation, or other binding official act, or unconditionally announced by the President, an authorized Cabinet official, or another authorized U.S. government body.

A new body or formally designated existing body qualifies only if a binding official action grants it primary nationwide, cross-sector AI rulemaking, licensing, supervisory, or enforcement authority comparable in substance to a national regulator, or if an unconditional official announcement commits to granting it such authority, including when that authority will take effect later. The body's name or form does not control: a council, office, standards body, or SRO qualifies if one identifiable body receives those powers. A body that only advises, coordinates, studies, tests, sets voluntary standards, conducts one-off reviews, or has only sector-specific authority does not qualify. Distributed sector-by-sector authority does not qualify.

title: Will the U.S. authorize a government AI kill switch before Jan 1, 2028?
subtitle: Before Jan 1, 2028
rules_primary: If federal legislation authorizing government-initiated AI shutdowns has become law after Issuance and before Jan 1, 2028, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_secondary:
A qualifying federal law must expressly authorize the U.S. government to initiate the shutdown, suspension, or technical disabling of an operating AI model or system to address safety or security risks or loss of control. The government may act directly or compel a developer, operator, or service provider to carry out the shutdown, including through a court order.

A company-controlled kill switch alone does not qualify. Neither does authority limited to blocking future development or release, or a general power to regulate AI without authority to stop an operating system. The government need not own or physically operate the shutdown mechanism, and the authority need not be used before the deadline. A later effective date does not delay qualification.

An example of this is the AI Kill Switch Act (H.R. 9917).

The statement must describe an achieved capability in which the company's AI autonomously conducts the research and development needed to materially improve the general capabilities of its most capable or near-frontier AI systems, or produce a more capable successor, with the improved system able to drive further such improvements.

Toy, narrow, sandboxed, proof-of-concept, prompt, skill, or benchmark-only improvements do not qualify. Humans may provide high-level goals, resources, oversight, and approval, but must not supply the substantive research choices or technical solution.

The capability must be affirmatively described as currently achieved in an official company communication or by an executive or research leader speaking about the company's capabilities. Future plans, speculation, offhand remarks, interviewer characterizations, leaks, model outputs, and third-party claims do not qualify.

A public release, named model, technical demonstration, or independent verification is not required.

title: Will Trump call for a global AI slowdown before Jan 1, 2027?
subtitle: Before Jan 1, 2027
rules_primary: If Donald Trump makes at least 1 statement explicitly calling for or endorsing a global pause, pacing, or slowdown in frontier AI development before Jan 1, 2027, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_secondary:
Pause, pacing, and slowdown include a temporary halt or a deliberate reduction in the rate of frontier AI research, training, or capability development; a complete halt is not required. Frontier AI means leading general-purpose AI systems and development of their successors. The call must concern development generally on a worldwide basis or through coordinated action across countries. Calls restricted to one sector or application, such as biology, or to one country do NOT qualify.

An explicit endorsement of a qualifying proposal counts, including a proposal conditional on reciprocal participation or safeguards. Merely describing, considering, or quoting a proposal without endorsing its slowdown component does NOT count. Deployment restrictions, safety measures, or regulation alone do NOT count without an explicit development slowdown call. Implementation is not required.

Statements must be affirmatively issued or signed; being quoted in another’s statement does not count. Retweets, reposts, or shares without additional commentary do not count as statements.

title: Will Trump officially rename AI before Oct 1, 2026?
subtitle: Before Oct 1, 2026
rules_primary: If Donald Trump formally adopts or directs adoption of a replacement name for Artificial Intelligence or AI for United States official use through a personally signed presidential action after Issuance and before Oct 1, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_secondary:
The qualifying action must be of the specific type designated (executive order, presidential memorandum, proclamation, directive, determination, or finding), be signed by the President personally during the specified time period, and explicitly address the topic in the document's operative provisions, title, or official White House summary. Actions must have legal or policy effect - ceremonial proclamations without policy impact do not qualify unless specifically included. Actions that only incidentally mention the topic, statements without formal action, actions by cabinet members, legislative proposals without executive action, and signing statements do not qualify. The action must be publicly announced or documented by a Source Agency before expiration.

The topic is the preexisting official designation Artificial Intelligence or AI for United States official use. Any replacement name qualifies. The action must adopt or direct adoption of the replacement for United States official use; an informal, honorary, or agency-only label does not qualify.

title: Will the U.S. and China agree to establish an AI hotline before Jan 1, 2027?
subtitle: Before Jan 1, 2027
rules_primary: If the governments of the United States and China have formally announced an agreement to establish, or have implemented, a bilateral notification mechanism for AI incidents that could affect national security after Issuance and before Jan 1, 2027, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_secondary:
Only reporting from any of the Source Agencies qualifies for the purposes of this market. Reports that merely reference prior publications (from before Issuance) do not qualify, unless the new article itself explicitly reaffirms the truth of the topic as of the publication date. Republishing of content originally produced by other sources (e.g., wire services) only qualifies if the content is hosted on the outlet's official platform and the outlet is clearly identified as the publishing entity.

A qualifying mechanism must be a government-to-government arrangement for notifying the other government about relevant AI incidents; general AI dialogue, shared principles, safety cooperation, or a general hotline without the incident-notification function does not satisfy this topic.

The mechanism must be expressly described in an official government announcement, agreement text, or qualifying Source Agency report as covering AI incidents with national-security implications. A general AI-incident channel does not qualify based solely on an inference that the incidents it covers could affect national security.

A formal announcement must appear in an official agreement text, communiqué, readout, press release, other written government statement, or a formal government press conference, briefing, leaders' summit, signing ceremony, or formal address. One government's official statement is sufficient only when it expressly states that both governments agreed. Informal remarks, press gaggles, a report of a proposal, an agreement to meet, or a transcript of those remarks alone does not qualify.

Implementation requires evidence that both governments have operationalized, activated, or used the bilateral notification mechanism. A unilateral proposal, ongoing negotiation, planned dialogue, generic AI-safety principles, company standards, private or unofficial arrangement, domestic-only system, or a mechanism unrelated to AI incidents affecting national security does not qualify. A broader AI-safety agreement qualifies only when it expressly adopts or implements this incident-notification component.

title: Will OpenAI release a personal AI agent before Jan 1, 2027?
subtitle: Before Jan 1, 2027
rules_primary: If an OpenAI product has implemented a general-purpose personal AI agent that remembers the user and starts multi-step tasks across third-party apps on its own before Jan 1, 2027, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_secondary:
The function must be live and processing user interactions, not explicitly labeled as "beta," "test," "experimental," "preview," or "early access" or similar, and officially acknowledged by the company through announcements, documentation, or help pages. Implementation includes direct integration into the product's interface, automatic application to user accounts, user-initiated activation through official controls, API implementation, or policy changes that operationally enforce the function. Announcements without deployment, employee-only testing, technical documentation without implementation, and third-party additions without authorization do not qualify. The implementation must occur in the United States unless otherwise specified. If it meets these conditions, it counts from the first date it is live for users outside the company, including in a gradual rollout or a waitlist, invitation-only, or paid-tier release.

A general-purpose personal AI agent acts for an individual user on that user's own goals, is not limited to a single category of task or app, such as only code, only documents, or only shopping, and (1) retains user-specific information, such as preferences, relationships, goals, or ongoing activities, across separate interactions, and (2) as a built-in capability, on its own initiative and outside any conversation or task the user has started, begins new multi-step actions across third-party apps, websites, or services to advance the user's ongoing goals, based on what it has retained. The agent must itself take at least one such action before asking the user anything, and may then pause for approval before a step such as sending a message or making a purchase. An action means changing something in a third-party app, website, or service on the user's behalf, such as sending, posting, booking, purchasing, submitting a form, or creating, editing, or deleting an item; reading, searching, or summarizing does not count. An agent focused on work qualifies if it acts across email, calendar, messaging, and the web for an individual user.

The following do not qualify: carrying out a task the user started, however long-running; running tasks on a user-defined schedule, event trigger, or monitor, or under a standing instruction that tells the agent what to do or which app, source, or workflow to watch; a briefing or notification on its own; a proposed task or suggestion that does nothing until the user accepts it; an offer made in reply to the user's message; memory alone; an agent configured by an organization to run shared team workflows; and a developer platform, SDK, or API for building agents, unless the company itself offers through it an agent that meets (1) and (2) for end users. A goal or preference the user has shared, from which the agent itself decides what new task to start, is not a standing instruction, and neither is turning the capability on, connecting apps, or granting permissions.

title: Will OpenAI release a personal AI agent before Oct 1, 2026?
subtitle: Before Oct 1, 2026
rules_primary: If an OpenAI product has implemented a general-purpose personal AI agent that remembers the user and starts multi-step tasks across third-party apps on its own before Oct 1, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_secondary:
The function must be live and processing user interactions, not explicitly labeled as "beta," "test," "experimental," "preview," or "early access" or similar, and officially acknowledged by the company through announcements, documentation, or help pages. Implementation includes direct integration into the product's interface, automatic application to user accounts, user-initiated activation through official controls, API implementation, or policy changes that operationally enforce the function. Announcements without deployment, employee-only testing, technical documentation without implementation, and third-party additions without authorization do not qualify. The implementation must occur in the United States unless otherwise specified. If it meets these conditions, it counts from the first date it is live for users outside the company, including in a gradual rollout or a waitlist, invitation-only, or paid-tier release.

A general-purpose personal AI agent acts for an individual user on that user's own goals, is not limited to a single category of task or app, such as only code, only documents, or only shopping, and (1) retains user-specific information, such as preferences, relationships, goals, or ongoing activities, across separate interactions, and (2) as a built-in capability, on its own initiative and outside any conversation or task the user has started, begins new multi-step actions across third-party apps, websites, or services to advance the user's ongoing goals, based on what it has retained. The agent must itself take at least one such action before asking the user anything, and may then pause for approval before a step such as sending a message or making a purchase. An action means changing something in a third-party app, website, or service on the user's behalf, such as sending, posting, booking, purchasing, submitting a form, or creating, editing, or deleting an item; reading, searching, or summarizing does not count. An agent focused on work qualifies if it acts across email, calendar, messaging, and the web for an individual user.

The following do not qualify: carrying out a task the user started, however long-running; running tasks on a user-defined schedule, event trigger, or monitor, or under a standing instruction that tells the agent what to do or which app, source, or workflow to watch; a briefing or notification on its own; a proposed task or suggestion that does nothing until the user accepts it; an offer made in reply to the user's message; memory alone; an agent configured by an organization to run shared team workflows; and a developer platform, SDK, or API for building agents, unless the company itself offers through it an agent that meets (1) and (2) for end users. A goal or preference the user has shared, from which the agent itself decides what new task to start, is not a standing instruction, and neither is turning the capability on, connecting apps, or granting permissions.

title: Will it be reported by any of the Source Agencies that Anthropic and the Holy See hold an in-person meeting before Jan 1, 2027?
subtitle: Before Jan 1, 2027
rules_primary: If Anthropic and the Holy See hold an in-person meeting after Issuance and before Jan 1, 2027, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_secondary:
Only reporting from any of the Source Agencies qualifies for the purposes of this market. Reports that merely reference prior publications (from before Issuance) do not qualify. Republishing of content originally produced by other sources (e.g., wire services) only qualifies if the content is hosted on the outlet's official platform and the outlet is clearly identified as the publishing entity.

The meeting must be deliberately convened, held in person, and attended by at least one Anthropic representative and at least one Holy See representative who both actively participate. An Anthropic representative is a co-founder, an executive officer, or any other person Anthropic sends to speak for the company. A Holy See representative is the Pope, a cardinal, or an official of the Secretariat of State, the Roman Curia, or a Vatican dicastery or pontifical academy, acting in an official capacity. A private audience, closed-door briefing, roundtable, or jointly convened event may qualify, and the meeting need not produce an agreement or statement. Only the part of a meeting held after Issuance counts; a meeting held entirely before Issuance does not qualify, even if reported afterward.

Phone or video contact, correspondence, chance encounters, exchanges limited to greetings, courtesies, or photo opportunities, and attendance at the same public event or conference without a separately arranged exchange between the two sides do not qualify. Meetings between Anthropic and theologians, scholars, clergy, or advisers who do not hold an official Holy See position do not qualify.

title: Which country will have the best LLM at the end of the decade?
subtitle: United States
rules_primary: If an AI lab based in the United States has the highest-ranked AI model on the applicable index at 10:00 AM ET on Dec 31, 2029, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_secondary: The Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index is used first, followed by Epoch AI's General ECI and LiveBench Overall under the fallback rules. The default leaderboard is used, excluding preliminary or provisional scores. Only the ranking at the stated time counts; leading earlier does not. Ties follow the contract's tiebreakers. A model counts for the country where its credited organization is headquartered or, for a division, subsidiary or brand, where its ultimate parent is headquartered (e.g., Google DeepMind counts for the United States). If that country is not listed, every market resolves No.

title: Will it be reported by any of the Source Agencies that Anthropic and the Holy See hold an in-person meeting before Jul 1, 2027?
subtitle: Before Jul 1, 2027
rules_primary: If Anthropic and the Holy See hold an in-person meeting after Issuance and before Jul 1, 2027, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_secondary:
Only reporting from any of the Source Agencies qualifies for the purposes of this market. Reports that merely reference prior publications (from before Issuance) do not qualify. Republishing of content originally produced by other sources (e.g., wire services) only qualifies if the content is hosted on the outlet's official platform and the outlet is clearly identified as the publishing entity.

The meeting must be deliberately convened, held in person, and attended by at least one Anthropic representative and at least one Holy See representative who both actively participate. An Anthropic representative is a co-founder, an executive officer, or any other person Anthropic sends to speak for the company. A Holy See representative is the Pope, a cardinal, or an official of the Secretariat of State, the Roman Curia, or a Vatican dicastery or pontifical academy, acting in an official capacity. A private audience, closed-door briefing, roundtable, or jointly convened event may qualify, and the meeting need not produce an agreement or statement. Only the part of a meeting held after Issuance counts; a meeting held entirely before Issuance does not qualify, even if reported afterward.

Phone or video contact, correspondence, chance encounters, exchanges limited to greetings, courtesies, or photo opportunities, and attendance at the same public event or conference without a separately arranged exchange between the two sides do not qualify. Meetings between Anthropic and theologians, scholars, clergy, or advisers who do not hold an official Holy See position do not qualify.

title: What will Sam Altman say during 2026 New York Times DealBook Summit originally scheduled for November 18, 2026?
subtitle: Valuation / IPO
rules_primary:
If 
 Sam Altman says Valuation / IPO as part of 2026 New York Times DealBook Summit originally scheduled for November 18, 2026
, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_secondary:
How this is resolved
Video of the 2026 New York Times DealBook Summit originally scheduled for November 18, 2026 using the original broadcast, stream, or official video release by The New York Times.
If a consensus by Kalshi employees cannot be reached using video, internal & external (official) transcripts of the 2026 New York Times DealBook Summit originally scheduled for November 18, 2026 will be used.

Payout Criteria
The exact phrase/word, or a plural or possessive form of the phrase/word. 
Plural nouns occurring within proper nouns and noun phrases (e.g. names, titles, etc).
Sam Altman speaking in an official capacity.
For phrases with slashes like "Doge/Dogecoin," either word satisfies the criterion.

Doesn't count for payout
Grammatical/tense inflections are otherwise not included. 
Presence alone during a livestream is not sufficient for the market to qualify (e.g., inaudible private conversations on camera, unofficial statements picked up on a hot mic).
Except as otherwise specified, previously aired content, archival footage, and recordings captured at times, places, or events wholly separate from the featured address.

Payout for cancellations and delays
If an event is definitively cancelled or the event fails to qualify under the Payout Criterion, or any other circumstance prevents normal resolution, then the market for "Event does not qualify" resolves to Yes and all other markets will resolve to No.  
If the event is postponed, and such a postponement is announced by the end of the following calendar day to be rescheduled to a time within 14 calendar days, the markets shall remain open.
